_note: Defect log maintained by the Test Engineer (STP 14.2). Execution defects were found by the automated suite in cycle 1 and retested in cycle 2. Review defects were found during static review of SRS v1.0 and STP v1.0.

execution_defects.title: HTTPS enforcement bypassed by a client-supplied X-Forwarded-Proto header
execution_defects.environment: APAS reference build, production configuration (ENFORCE_HTTPS=True), Flask test client over plain HTTP
execution_defects.description: The HTTPS check treated any request carrying the header X-Forwarded-Proto: https as secure, even when no reverse proxy is deployed. A client on plain HTTP could therefore submit credentials and receive a session token over an unencrypted connection.
steps: Start APAS with the production configuration (no reverse proxy).
Send POST http://<host>/api/auth/login with a valid username/password and the header X-Forwarded-Proto: https.
Send GET http://<host>/dashboard with the same header.
execution_defects.expected: POST rejected with HTTP 403 "HTTPS is required"; GET redirected to https:// with HTTP 301.
execution_defects.actual: POST returned HTTP 200 with a session token over plain HTTP; GET was served (HTTP 302 to /login) instead of being redirected to HTTPS.
execution_defects.evidence: results/cycle1/execution_results.json (TC-SEC-03.3: 'spoofed GET -> HTTP 302; spoofed POST login -> HTTP 200')
execution_defects.resolution: The header is now honoured only when TRUST_PROXY=True, through werkzeug ProxyFix (x_proto=1). Otherwise only the real connection scheme (request.is_secure) is used.
execution_defects.retest: TC-SEC-03.3 passed in cycle 2 (GET 301, POST 403). Regression: TC-SEC-03.1/03.2 and all suites passed.

execution_defects.title: Administrator overview dashboard exceeds the 3-second response target under concurrent load
execution_defects.module: Reporting and Dashboard Service / Authentication Service (apas/api.py student_overview, apas/security.py current_user)
execution_defects.environment: APAS on HTTPS (werkzeug threaded server), SQLite, 306 students (~42 000 grade/attendance rows), 10 concurrent clients, MacBook (darwin)
execution_defects.description: With 10 concurrent users, the 95th-percentile response time of the administrator overview dashboard (GET /api/dashboard as admin) was 4.19 s, with a maximum of 7.10 s. Overall p95 across all dashboards was 2.74 s, but one dashboard type broke the APAS-NF-001 target.
steps: Seed the test data plus 300 synthetic students (apas.seed.add_synthetic_students).
Run APAS over HTTPS and log in as admin, fac.rao and aarav.
Send 300 dashboard requests (6 dashboard types, 50 each) from 10 concurrent threads.
Compute the 95th percentile per dashboard type.
execution_defects.expected: 95th percentile <= 3.0 s for every dashboard type.
execution_defects.actual: admin API overview p95 = 4.189 s (max 7.102 s); faculty API overview p95 = 2.994 s (close to the limit).
execution_defects.root_cause: (1) Every overview request re-analysed all 306 students, even when nothing had changed. (2) Every authenticated request wrote sessions.last_seen, so concurrent read-only requests queued for SQLite's single write lock.
execution_defects.resolution: Overview results are cached per database and invalidated through a data_version counter maintained by triggers on students/subjects/grades/attendance/config. The session last_seen timestamp is written at most once per 60 s.
execution_defects.retest: Cycle 2 retest at the team load profile TD-12 (50 concurrent users, stricter than cycle 1): TC-PERF-01.1 overall p95 0.46 s (max 0.54 s); TC-PERF-01.2 with concurrent grade writes p95 0.90 s. New regression test TC-VIS-01.5 confirms the cache is invalidated immediately after a grade change.

test_script_corrections.description: First dry run: 169 of 189 tests returned HTTP 301 because the test client did not send requests over https:// (werkzeug ignores environ_base['wsgi.url_scheme']). The application behaved correctly by redirecting plain HTTP.
test_script_corrections.correction: Added the https_client() fixture, which defaults base_url to https://localhost. The dry run is not counted as an execution cycle.

test_script_corrections.description: The expected result for an 18-month retention period omitted the 12-months-2-days entry, which is correctly retained because it is younger than 18 months.
test_script_corrections.correction: Expected result corrected to keep 30d, 11m29d, 12m2d and 13m.

test_script_corrections.description: After the expected 'append-only' error, the test's own database connection kept an open transaction. The application's next write timed out on the lock and returned HTTP 500.
test_script_corrections.correction: The test now rolls back after the rejected UPDATE.

review_defects.title: Risk and performance thresholds are not specified
review_defects.description: F-009 refers to 'configured thresholds' and F-014 to 'predefined risk criteria' without numeric values, so expected results cannot be derived from the SRS.
review_defects.impact: Testers had to assume values: attendance < 75%, overall performance < 50%, failed subject < 40%; high risk = predicted SGPA < 5.0 or attendance < 65%; medium risk = predicted SGPA < 6.0 or attendance < 75%.
review_defects.recommendation: Add default threshold values and state whether comparisons are strict (<) or inclusive (<=). Boundary tests TC-ANA-03.1 / TC-PRED-02.1 assume strict '<'.

review_defects.title: Assignment submission tracking has no functional requirement or test case
review_defects.document: SRS v1.0 sections 1.2 and 2.2 vs section 4 / RTM
review_defects.description: Scope (1.2) and Major Product Functions (2.2) include 'Assignment submission and marks tracking', but no requirement from APAS-F-001 to F-015 and no RTM row covers it.
review_defects.impact: This function is untraceable and untested. The current build models only ISA/ESA assessments.
review_defects.recommendation: Either add a functional requirement (e.g. APAS-F-016) with acceptance criteria and a test case, or remove the function from the scope.

review_defects.title: 'Normal operating conditions' for the response-time target are not quantified
review_defects.description: The 3-second target has no defined concurrent-user count, data volume or network conditions.
review_defects.impact: Cycle 1 assumed 10 concurrent users. Cycle 2 uses the team test-data profile TD-12 (50 concurrent users, 306 students), which is still not an SRS-approved figure.
review_defects.recommendation: Define the load profile (e.g. N concurrent users, M students, request mix) in the SRS or STP.

review_defects.title: No acceptance criterion for prediction quality
review_defects.description: F-013 requires predictions to be 'generated and displayed' but sets no accuracy or error bound. The STP correctly forbids inventing one.
review_defects.impact: TC-PRED-01.4 can only report MAE/RMSE/precision/recall, not pass or fail on accuracy.
review_defects.recommendation: Agree a target (e.g. MAE <= 0.5 SGPA on historical data) or record that prediction quality is informational only.

review_defects.title: RTM maps two different requirements to the same test case TC-SEC-01
review_defects.description: APAS-NF-003 (access restricted by role and permission) and APAS-SR-001 (valid credentials required) both map only to TC-SEC-01. NF-003 is about authorisation, which TC-SEC-02 covers.
review_defects.impact: Role-based restriction under NF-003 is not traceable to the RBAC test case.
review_defects.recommendation: Map APAS-NF-003 to TC-SEC-01 and TC-SEC-02 (as done in the execution RTM).

review_defects.title: SRS allows plain HTTP, which contradicts APAS-SR-003
review_defects.description: Section 3.4 says communication 'shall use HTTP or HTTPS', while SR-003 requires HTTPS with TLS 1.2+ and requires insecure connections to be rejected or redirected.
review_defects.impact: Ambiguous whether HTTP is acceptable anywhere.
review_defects.recommendation: State that HTTP is permitted only in local development environments without real student data.

review_defects.title: Session timeout and account-lockout policy are not specified
review_defects.description: The SRS requires secure sessions but does not define an idle timeout or a brute-force lockout policy.
review_defects.impact: The test build assumes a 30-minute idle timeout and a 15-minute lockout after 5 failed logins (TC-AUTH-03.3, TC-AUTH-01.6).
review_defects.recommendation: Add explicit values to the SRS security requirements.

review_defects.title: Table text appears cut off in the SRS
review_defects.description: Text extracted from the 'Comments / Dependencies' column ends mid-word: 'Requires session mana' (F-003) and 'reporting servic' (F-012). This suggests the table cells overflow the page.
review_defects.recommendation: Check visually and widen or rewrap the table columns.

review_defects.title: Inconsistent document metadata
review_defects.document: SRS v1.0 revision history; STP v1.0 section 15.3
review_defects.description: The SRS revision history lists '1.0, 18-08-2025, Instructor, SRS with diagrams embedded' (template leftover), while the document is dated 12-10-2026 by Team 05. The STP approval table says 'To be assigned' although section 9 names the QA Lead (Neha Rastogi) and Project Lead (Pallavi B).
review_defects.recommendation: Remove the template row and fill in the approval table with the assigned names.
